Summaries, Predictions and Other Methods for nbreg Fits

Source: R/methods-nbreg.R
nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard methods for objects returned by nbreg(): printing, summaries with a coefficient table, extracting coefficients, the variance-covariance matrix, the log-likelihood (with a df attribute, so AIC() and BIC() work), fitted values, residuals, the number of observations, and predictions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("link", "response"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  offset = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

An nbreg fit (or, for print.summary.nbreg(), its summary).

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Not used.

type

For residuals(): "response" (\(y - \hat\mu\)) or "pearson" (the response residual times the square root of the prior weight, divided by the estimated standard deviation \(\sqrt{\hat\mu + \hat\mu^2/\hat\theta}\)). For predict(): "link" (the linear predictor, on the log scale) or "response" (the expected count).

newdata

Optional data frame of covariate values for predict(). If omitted, predictions are for the data used in the fit.

se.fit

Logical; if TRUE, predict() also returns standard errors. On the link scale they are \(\sqrt{x^\top V x}\); on the response scale they are \(\hat\mu\) times that (the delta method). They treat theta as known, like the coefficient standard errors.

offset

For predict() with newdata, only when the model was fitted with the offset argument: the offset values for the new rows. Needed when the original offset cannot be recomputed from newdata (for example when it was a stand-alone numeric vector). Offsets written as offset() terms in the formula are always taken from newdata.

Value

coef() a named vector; vcov() a matrix; logLik() an object of class logLik; fitted() and residuals() numeric vectors; nobs() the number of observations with positive weight; predict() a numeric vector, or with se.fit = TRUE a list with elements fit and se.fit; summary() an object of class summary.nbreg; the print methods return their argument invisibly.

Details

Fitted values and residuals follow na.action: with stats::na.exclude() they are padded with NA to the length of the original data.

For predict() with newdata and a model fitted with the offset argument, the original offset expression is re-evaluated in newdata when it refers to at least one of its columns (for example offset = log(t) with a column t). Otherwise the offset for the new rows must be supplied with offset =; it is never silently reused from the fit.

See also

nbreg()

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:8, y = c(1, 0, 6, 1, 9, 2, 20, 4))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Negative binomial regression (NB2, log link)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>     -0.1133       0.3440  
#> 
#> Theta: 1.509 (SE 1.025)
#> Log-likelihood: -20.3448 on 3 df;  AIC: 46.6896
#> Observations: 8
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -0.9033 -0.8066 -0.4540  0.9408  1.3534 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> (Intercept)  -0.1133     0.8416  -0.135    0.893  
#> x             0.3440     0.1545   2.226    0.026 *
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.509 (SE 1.025)
#> Log-likelihood: -20.3448 on 3 df
#> AIC: 46.6896;  BIC: 46.9279
#> Observations: 8;  residual df: 6
#> Outer passes: 4;  converged: yes
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>  -0.1133373   0.3439702 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 46.68958
residuals(fit, type = "pearson")
#>          1          2          3          4          5          6          7 
#> -0.1706543 -0.9032882  1.3533650 -0.7374040  0.8667084 -0.7976279  1.1631452 
#>          8 
#> -0.8334357 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(2.5, 9)), type = "response",
        se.fit = TRUE)
#> $fit
#>        1        2 
#>  2.10979 19.73502 
#> 
#> $se.fit
#>         1         2 
#>  1.082476 13.993150 
#>
